subject: Quantized econ anchor & incentive request — MLScale discovery follow-up
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@mlscale.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Quantized econ anchor & incentive request — MLScale discovery follow-up

Hi Alyssa — great to meet you and the MLScale team earlier today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have a shared anchor for economics and incentives.

Recap from the call (short):
- Primary workload: user-facing assistants + a batch summarization job for ingestion.
- Peak inference profile: estimates you gave ~10M tokens/day (spiky), average ~6M tokens/day -> ~180M tokens/month baseline. You mentioned a pilot month could spike to ~350M tokens.
- Key asks: aggressive unit price for the pilot, clear committed-use path if MLScale needs steady capacity, and a startup credit if you qualify. Also procurement will want an explicit AUP/data residency note.

Unit-econ targets you mentioned in the call: $/1M tokens target ~ $600–$800 for year 1 (your preferred target $600). You also asked about multi-year step-downs and whether startup credits stack with committed discounts.

Our proposed next steps from Redwood:
1) Ben will assemble 2 pricing scenarios (pilot-focused and 12mo committed) and show the blended effective $/1M tokens.
2) Monica will map contracting path (startup program eligibility, SOW + standard MSA redline timeline).
3) We’ll attach a short proposal and your monthly projection template so we can align on numbers.

Quick economic anchors (initial thinking — placeholder until Ben runs exact calc):
- Hosted baseline (no commit): ~$1,200 / 1M tokens for the model family we discussed (high-capacity open model + streaming).
- 6mo committed-use (prepay or monthly invoice): ~20% discount off baseline -> effective ~$960 / 1M.
- 12mo committed-use: ~30% discount -> effective ~$840 / 1M.
- Multi-year (24+ months / expand): additional negotiated tail discount (we can model an extra 8–12% on top).
- Startup program: one-time credit (typical range $10k–$50k depending on eligibility) that can be applied to first invoices; credits stack with committed discounts in most cases.

We want to be explicit about how we’ll get you toward your $600 target. If MLScale can commit to a steady 300M tokens/month over 12 months and prepay/commit, we can explore an introductory proposal that brings effective $/1M closer to your target (Ben will run exact numbers).

Attachments: redwood-proposal-v1.pdf (proposal stub), mlscale-monthly-projection.csv (fill this with your expected monthly volumes and spike months).

Immediate asks for you: please confirm the average vs spike monthly profile you expect for months 1–6 and whether you have any hard budget ceilings for Q3.

I’ll leave the pricing math to Ben but wanted to capture the ask and next steps so nothing is missed.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
[Attachment: redwood-proposal-v1.pdf (PDF)]
[Attachment: mlscale-monthly-projection.csv (CSV)]

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@mlscale.io>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@mlscale.io
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quantized econ anchor & incentive request — MLScale discovery follow-up

Thanks Naomi — helpful summary and I appreciate the clear next steps. A couple clarifications from my side before Ben runs scenarios: 

- The 6–12 month profile we expect: months 1–2 pilot ~100–350M (high variance), months 3–6 steadying to ~180–220M, target steady-state months 7+ at ~250–300M.
- Budget range for pilot: $8k–$30k for month 1 depending on spikes. For runway planning we are trying to keep incremental monthly spend under $40k in Q3 as a hard ceiling.
- On the $/1M target: our internal target for negotiated pricing for year 1 is $600 / 1M — we realize that may need a combination of credits + commit to hit that, but please flag if that’s not feasible for the model family we discussed.

Procurement asks: can Redwood provide a one-pager on credit stacking and any minimums for startup program eligibility? Also, do you support quarterly true-ups if our usage is bursty?

I’ll review the attachments and fill in the projection CSV tonight. Looping procurement on the CC for contract timelines.

Best,
Alyssa Chen
Head of Product, MLScale
alyssa@mlscale.io
[Procurement contact: procurement@mlscale.io]

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 11:28:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing scenarios for MLScale (initial matrix)

Naomi / Monica — per Naomi’s recap and Alyssa’s profile, I ran two compact scenarios. Paste below as a quick anchor; I’ll push a spreadsheet to the Drive link once we iterate.

Scenario definitions (blended effective $/1M tokens):
- Baseline hosted (no commit): list price ~ $1,200 / 1M tokens.
- Pilot offer (month 1 spike protection): 15% off list for month 1 + $25k startup credit applied to invoice -> if month 1 usage = 300M tokens, invoice delta after credit ~ (300 * 1,200/1M * 0.85) - 25k ≈ $290k - 25k = $265k -> effective ~$883 / 1M for month 1 in that example.
- 6mo committed-use (steady 200M/mo): 20% off list -> effective $960 / 1M.
- 12mo committed-use (steady 300M/mo): 30% off list -> effective $840 / 1M.
- 12mo prepay option: additional 10% off the committed discount for payment-in-advance -> effective ~$756 / 1M (for 12mo, prepay).
- Multi-year add-on: negotiate an extra 8–12% after year 2 depending on expansion cadence.

To get to Alyssa’s $600 / 1M target we could consider a combined structure: 12mo prepay at high commit (300M+/mo) + one-time startup credit + attribution of reserved slot discounts -> approximates $600–$700 / 1M if MLScale is willing to prepay and commit to growth milestones. I’ll flag the component that moves the needle: prepay & multi-year commitment.

Next internal ask: Monica, can you confirm standard startup credit bands and whether our legal team needs a special clause for credit stacking? If yes, we’ll prepare the MSA addendum language.

I’ll upload a fully worked spreadsheet to the Drive link by EOD Monday with a few sensitivity rows (pilot spike, 6mo steady, 12mo steady).

—Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 (646) 555-0123
[Attachment: pricing-matrix-draft.xlsx (placeholder, working doc on Drive)]

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@mlscale.io>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quantized econ anchor & incentive request — MLScale discovery follow-up

Thanks — that gives us a concrete place to have an internal conversation. I’ll take Ben’s anchors and run them by finance and our CEO this week. Two quick asks before we book next touch: 

1) Could you prepare a short SOW template that describes the pilot acceptance criteria (latency SLOs, token logging retention, rollback policy) and an estimated implementation timeline?
2) Please include a clear statement on credit stacking and how prepay interacts with startup credits (one-line policy is fine).

If we’re aligned, can we book a 30-min sync for Thu, Jun 3 (PDT) to review the spreadsheet and an initial SOW? I’m available 10:00–12:00 PDT.

If you can get the spreadsheet + SOW stub to me by Wed EOD that will help speed the procurement review.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — speak soon.

Best,
Alyssa
Head of Product | MLScale
alyssa@mlscale.io
[Next step: schedule 30-min review on Thu, Jun 3 10:30 PDT — tentative]
